clue.text: Bird bites when upset — not good

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the next piece
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to gnaw is to bite, so bites gives gnaws

explanation.surface: A bird that has been annoyed starts pecking, which is bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns GNAWS over to SWANG, and 'not good' drops its G.
explanation.definitionFit: The swan is a large long-necked water bird, so it is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Wrap up piece of plumbing emerging from bathroom?

definitions.meaning: to wrap up, in slang, is to stop talking, to be quiet

definitions.text: piece of plumbing emerging from bathroom?
definitions.meaning: read literally, a pipe going down out of the bathroom, the waste pipe

explanation.surface: A plumber is told to finish the job on a pipe coming out of a bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second reading is a whimsical literal split of the phrase into PIPE and DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Both 'wrap up' and the answer are informal orders to stop talking and be quiet.

clue.text: Kipling's soldier, say, making a speech?

indicators.note: making here means that the letter is turned into something else, so one letter gets swapped for a word

parts.note: a talk is a speech

explanation.surface: A question about whether one of Kipling's military men is giving an address.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'say, making a speech' as SAY with its letter A made into TALK. Stalky is the hero of Kipling's school stories Stalky & Co., who later becomes a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling wrote about Stalky as a schoolboy who grew up to be an army officer in India.

clue.text: Routine has to be organised for discipline in the home

indicators.note: letters that are organised are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Domestic discipline needs an organised routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be organised' rearranges ROUTINE plus HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To housetrain a pet is to teach it clean habits indoors, a kind of domestic training.

clue.text: It's frightening crossing lake — cover needed

indicators.note: the frightening word goes across the lake, so it lies around it

parts.note: cowing means intimidating, frightening

explanation.surface: Something scary is crossing a lake, so a protective cover is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts L inside COWING.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowling is the removable metal casing over an engine, especially on an aircraft.

clue.text: Gosh — you can hear that army unit!

indicators.note: what is heard is a spoken sound, so the answer is said like the exclamation

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the noise an army unit makes.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is said 'core', its P and S silent, just like COR.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is a military formation made up of several divisions.

clue.text: Naughty girl once got to tour the French educational establishment

indicators.note: touring goes round something, so the jumbled letters surround the French article
naughty suggests misbehaving, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A badly behaved girl once got to go on a tour of a French college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' rearranges GIRL ONCE GOT, and 'to tour' wraps it round LE. Girton is a college of Cambridge University, founded for women.
explanation.definitionFit: Girton College is part of Cambridge University, so it is a place of learning.

clue.text: Nothing right about politician's blast

indicators.note: about means turned round, so these letters read backwards

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A politician's outburst has nothing right in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns O and RT round to TRO. The blog notes a trompe is strictly the apparatus that makes a blast of air for a furnace.
explanation.definitionFit: A tromp is a water-driven device for producing a blast of air for a furnace, standing loosely for the blast itself.

clue.text: Victim outside a church inclined to be moralistic

indicators.note: the victim is placed outside, around the other letters

parts.note: prey is a victim

explanation.surface: A victim stands outside a church whose sermons are rather moralistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Preachy describes someone who lectures others on morals, like a tiresome preacher.

clue.text: Boundary made by iron-clad circle

indicators.note: clad means covered, so the iron letters go around the circle

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A boundary marked by an armoured ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron-clad' reads as one adjective, but it splits: the iron is clad round the circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe is the outer edge or margin of something, its border.

clue.text: Enjoyed something of historic interest — small building for Caesar originally

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one piece swaps in where another was

parts.note: a relic is an object surviving from the past

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: a shed is a small building

explanation.surface: Someone enjoyed visiting a historic site, a small building used by Julius Caesar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caesar originally' looks like a Roman history note, but it only names the letter C to be swapped out.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish something is to take great pleasure in it, so relished is enjoyed.

clue.text: Son imprisoned in city saying sorry — how to end confinement?

indicators.note: the son is locked up inside the city letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
an apology is a saying sorry

explanation.surface: A son jailed in the City apologises, wondering how to get out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned in' puts S inside EC. The definition, with its question mark, describes the escape artist's skill playfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapology is the art of freeing oneself from chains and locks, as Houdini did.

clue.text: Physical problem? Somehow get calmer with yoga

indicators.note: somehow suggests an unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice that yoga will make you calmer about a health issue.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal sits at the front of the clue and works on CALMER and YOGA; 'get' and 'with' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Acromegaly is a hormonal disorder causing enlarged hands, feet and face, a bodily condition.

clue.text: Food that a racehorse needs

definitions.meaning: ... is food, as in hard ..., ship's biscuit
the saddle, bridle and other riding gear a horse wears

explanation.surface: Feeding a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardtack is plain fare for sailors, and a horse's saddlery is collectively called its tack.

clue.text: Drama about charge included in bill presented by any big firm?

indicators.note: about means around, so the drama letters surround the rest

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial display, drama

indicators.note: the charge sits inside the bill

parts.note: AC, account, is a bill
rent is a charge for hiring

explanation.surface: A dispute over a fee on an invoice from some major firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the playful definition: a parent company is the big firm that owns smaller offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent company owns subsidiaries, so it is a large business group at the top.

clue.text: Endless crush preceding time signal

indicators.note: endless means losing the last letter

parts.note: to press is to crush
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A crowded crush before a time signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'signal' is a verb here, to give warning of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To presage is to foreshadow or portend, giving a warning sign of something to come.

clue.text: Protestant version of Bible, one got hold of by converted Roman

indicators.note: the jumbled Roman holds the other letters inside
converted means changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
I, the Roman numeral, is one

explanation.surface: A Roman converted to Protestantism takes up a Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The Moravian Church is a Protestant denomination that began in Bohemia and Moravia, now in the Czech Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moravian Church is an old Protestant denomination, so a member is a Protestant.

clue.text: The female's modelling initially for statue

parts.note: her means belonging to a woman

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

explanation.surface: A woman's early modelling work for a statue.
explanation.definitionFit: A herm is a square pillar topped by a carved head, originally of Hermes, a kind of sculpture.

clue.text: Results in onset of sweat possibly?

definitions.text: Results in onset of sweat possibly?

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement of these letters
onset means beginning, so take the first letter

explanation.surface: Something that brings you out in a sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges RESULTS IN; 'onset of' gives S from 'sweat'. The whole clue is the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: Sultry weather is hot and humid, and that sticky heat is what makes people sweat.

clue.text: Won't you primarily sing this at sea?

parts.note: shan't, shall not, is a refusal like won't

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether they'll refuse to sing on board.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stretches 'sing this at sea' to the song itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a work song sung by sailors as they haul ropes.

clue.text: Cut flower deprived of root

indicators.note: in a down clue the root is the bottom, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Severn

explanation.surface: A flower is cut, losing its root.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river (it flows): the Severn, Britain's longest river. 'deprived of root' drops its last letter, the foot of a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever something is to cut it off or apart.

clue.text: Noble fellow hurt and sombre

parts.note: to mar is to damage, hurt
grave means serious, sombre

explanation.surface: A nobleman who is wounded and in a serious mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A margrave was a German nobleman ruling a border province, roughly a marquess.

clue.text: Case about to be dismissed in fulfilment of solemn promise

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: the vocative is a grammatical case, used to address someone
CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A legal case about to be thrown out over a vow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks legal but is grammatical: VOCATIVE loses CA by 'to be dismissed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A votive offering is one given to fulfil a vow made to a god or saint.

clue.text: Ultimately reject bad work

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter

parts.note: ill means bad

explanation.surface: In the end, poor work is rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: To till the soil is to work the land by ploughing or digging it.

clue.text: Yarn about Conservative making comeback brings applause

indicators.note: coming back means turning round, read backwards
about means around, so the story is placed around the party letter

parts.note: a yarn is a tale, a story

explanation.surface: A story about a Tory politician's return wins applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts C inside TALE to make TALCE, and 'making comeback' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant success or acclaim, the warm reception that applause expresses.

clue.text: One helps others learn and be free

indicators.note: letters set free are loosened into a new order

explanation.surface: A teacher helps people learn and be free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges LEARN and BE.
explanation.definitionFit: An enabler is a person who makes it possible for someone else to do something.
